speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think I'm one of the last speakers that is standing between you and the long weekend.
zh: 我想我是最后几位演讲者之一，站在你们和长周末之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I hope I can get your energy levels up.
zh: 所以我希望我能让大家的精神振作起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm responsible for our internal AI tools for our sales team.
zh: 我负责我们销售团队的内部 AI 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason I'm here today is, indeed, we launched our internal go-to-market assistant in September last year.
zh: 我今天在这里的原因是，我们确实在去年 9 月上线了我们的内部 go-to-market 助手。

speaker: Unknown
en: It answered more than one million questions so far.
zh: 它到目前为止已经回答了超过一百万个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have roughly answered 40,000 questions a week.
zh: 我们每周大约回答 40,000 个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are the customer zero for all of Snowflake products.
zh: 而且我们是所有 Snowflake 产品的 customer zero(零号客户)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is build on Snowflake co-work.
zh: 这是构建在 Snowflake co-work 上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I meet a lot of customers every week, okay?
zh: 我每周都会见很多客户，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I meet a lot of enterprises, Fortune 500 companies, and then they're all trying to build similar things, and they all struggle, right?
zh: 我会见到很多企业、财富 500 强公司，他们都在尝试构建类似的东西，而且他们都很挣扎，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, and then I end up, like, having this discussion with them all the time.
zh: 所以，我最后总是要和他们进行这样的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, they ask, like, how did you guys do it?
zh: 比如，他们会问，你们是怎么做到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we share our best practices.
zh: 然后我们分享我们的最佳实践。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I will try to share some of those things with you.
zh: 所以我会尝试与你们分享其中的一些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm told that I need to have some code in my presentation.
zh: 有人告诉我在演示中要有一些代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't, but I will try to show you at least some architectural diagrams, just to make it more interesting for the engineering audience.
zh: 我没有代码，但我会至少给你们展示一些架构图，好让工程听众觉得更有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: But let's jump into it.
zh: 但让我们直接开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think before we start, like I think I already, I was watching the other presentations, like I think everyone tries to give their interpretation of like, you know, why are we even building things for go-to-market, okay?
zh: 我想在开始之前，我想我已经——我看了其他几场演讲，我想每个人都在给出自己的解读，解释我们到底为什么要为 go-to-market 构建东西，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is how I explain it to family and friends.
zh: 我就是这样向家人和朋友解释的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's take Snowflake, okay?
zh: 那我们就拿 Snowflake 来说，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are a company of like, you know, close to 10,000 people.
zh: 我们是一家有差不多 10,000 名员工的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you look at our organization, almost half of our basically workforce is sales, right?
zh: 如果你看看我们的组织，几乎一半的基本员工队伍都是销售，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are they responsible for?
zh: 那他们负责什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're responsible for revenue generation.
zh: 他们负责创造营收。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they struggle with?
zh: 他们在为什么而挣扎？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I talk to a lot of customers.
zh: 我和很多客户交谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very common.
zh: 这很常见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's data is siloed.
zh: 每个人的数据都是孤岛。

speaker: Unknown
en: We work with a lot of first-party data, a lot of third-party data.
zh: 我们使用很多第一方数据、很多第三方数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all locked down in these SaaS tools and things like that.
zh: 这些数据全都被锁在这些 SaaS 工具之类的东西里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And literally, we have, for example, wraps who are using 15 different tools, not because they love the UI of those tools, because every tool has a different data point, and then they end up stitching all of that together in spreadsheets and running it there, right?
zh: 字面意义上，我们有，比如，wraps 在使用 15 种不同的工具，不是因为他们喜欢那些工具的界面，而是因为每个工具都有不同的数据点，然后他们最后要把所有这些在电子表格里拼接起来，在那上面运行，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the data is endless.
zh: 然后数据是无止境的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we have reps who have 1,000 accounts assigned to them, 1,000 customers.
zh: 比如我们有销售代表被分配了 1,000 个客户账户、1,000 个客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to stay on top of their recent news, what's happening with their consumption, did they get in support tickets recently, what was their latest earning results, everything.
zh: 他们必须随时掌握他们的最新新闻、他们的消费情况如何、他们最近有没有提交支持工单、他们最新的财报业绩是什么，所有一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not a single human on this planet can stay on top of that much data.
zh: 这个星球上没有一个人能跟得上那么多的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they need to do that 30 times, 40 times a day, right?
zh: 然后他们每天需要做这样的事情 30 次、40 次，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So what has AI offered for them?
zh: 那么 AI 为他们提供了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It offers data democratization, no more like thousand dashboards, no more access to analysts.
zh: 它提供了数据民主化，不再需要上千个仪表盘，不再需要去找分析师获取数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It offers automation possibilities for them.
zh: 它为他们提供了自动化的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It frees up their inbox.
zh: 它把他们的收件箱解放出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It offers tool consolidation, no longer 15 different tools that I need to work for.
zh: 它提供了工具整合，不再需要为 15 种不同的工具而工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that brings productivity savings.
zh: 而这带来了生产力上的节省。

speaker: Unknown
en: It frees up your time.
zh: 它解放了你的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can use that time on other things.
zh: 你可以把那些时间用在其他事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It helps you become a better seller.
zh: 它帮助你成为更好的销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are more effective with your customers.
zh: 你对客户更加高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that translates to business results.
zh: 而这转化为业务成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can cover more of your book.
zh: 你可以覆盖你客户名册中更多的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have better win rates.
zh: 你可以获得更好的赢单率。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have shorter deal cycles.
zh: 你可以拥有更短的成交周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, what everyone cares about, you can get incremental revenue.
zh: 而最终，每个人在意的，你能获得增量收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the reason why I'm working for making the go-to-market organizations more effective.
zh: 这就是我致力于让 go-to-market 组织更高效的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a catch.
zh: 但有一个陷阱。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are non-deterministic systems.
zh: 这些是非确定性系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I run into this problem every time with users.
zh: 我每次都会和用户遇到这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see many, many, many AI projects failed, and then it fails on this principle.
zh: 我见过很多很多很多 AI 项目失败，而且都是败在这个原则上。

speaker: Unknown
en: User trust is earned extremely hard, and it's lost overnight.
zh: 用户信任极难赢得，却能在一夜之间失去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So at the end, what you are doing is you are putting a free-form chat box there.
zh: 所以说到底，你做的事情就是放一个自由格式的聊天框在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And people will come in, and they will ask any question they can think of.
zh: 人们会过来，问出他们能想到的任何问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they like what they see in the first five questions, they come back.
zh: 如果他们喜欢前五个问题看到的答案，他们会回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they don't like what they see, it's 10 times more effort for you to win them back, if you can ever win them back, right?
zh: 如果他们不喜欢看到的答案，你要花十倍的功夫才能赢回他们——如果你还能赢回来的话，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a saying in our team, we say quality is P minus one, right?
zh: 所以我们团队有一句话，我们说质量是 P 减一，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's basically, we take that very, very seriously.
zh: 基本上，我们对这一点非常非常重视。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things that we really cared about is when I first joined the team,
zh: 所以我们真正在乎的事情之一是，我当初刚加入团队的时候，

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the team had all these like data sources connected from our top dashboards.
zh: 你知道，团队已经从我们的顶级仪表板接入了所有这些数据源。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a knowledge assistant built into it and so on.
zh: 我们内置了一个知识助手等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had three lines of agent instructions.
zh: 我们有三行智能体指令。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then before I even tried the agent, I opened the spreadsheet, I took the sales process, I wrote down 150 questions.
zh: 然后在我还没试过这个智能体之前，我打开电子表格，对照销售流程，写下了 150 个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the sales, our engineering team was like, what are you doing?
zh: 然后销售团队、我们的工程团队就说，你在干什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have that data in the agent.
zh: 智能体里没有那些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, it doesn't matter.
zh: 我说，没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the questions your sellers are gonna ask.
zh: 这些就是你们的销售人员会问的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we run our task, 50% accuracy, you know, like everyone's depressed and so on.
zh: 然后我们跑任务，50% 的准确率，你知道，大家都挺沮丧的之类。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we said, okay, let's make sure that we don't go for coverage, but we go for quality.
zh: 所以我们说，好，我们确保不追求覆盖面，而是追求质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to try to answer 100 questions and get them 70% right.
zh: 我们不想尝试回答 100 个问题，却只有 70% 答对。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to answer 50 questions, but get them 95% right.
zh: 我们想回答 50 个问题，但 95% 答对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because with that, you get the first impression, good first impression, you build the trust with them.
zh: 因为这样，你能得到第一印象，好的第一印象，你和他们建立起信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then rather than being in that boat of, oh, this thing doesn't work, people are like, oh, this thing is awesome.
zh: 然后与其处在那种境地——哦，这东西不好使——人们会说，哦，这东西太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I get more of that?
zh: 我能要更多吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started small, and 60% of the data we actually edit after the launch, after the six, seven months post-launch.
zh: 所以我们从小处开始，实际上 60% 的数据是我们在上线之后、上线后六七个月时才编辑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, if you look into our agent, I mean, it's not a small agent.
zh: 今天，如果你看我们的智能体，我的意思是，它不是一个小智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have 15 semantic views, 85 tables, 3,000 columns of data.
zh: 我们有 15 个语义视图、85 张表、3,000 列数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have, like, five to six different MCP connections on it, you know, close to 20 skills connected to that, and so on and so on, right?
zh: 我们在上面接了大概五六个不同的 MCP 连接，你知道，接近 20 个技能连在上面，等等等等，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a huge system that we are managing in here.
zh: 所以这是我们在管理的一个庞大系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you cannot just launch these things to everyone, right?
zh: 然后你不能直接把这些东西发布给所有人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we said that, look, we need to do this in a controlled way because we want to make sure that we earn that first five questions.
zh: 所以我们说，听着，我们需要以受控的方式来做这件事，因为我们要确保赢得那前五个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to burn our bridges in that first five questions, right?
zh: 我们不想在那前五个问题上把自己的桥烧掉，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why with every product we do, we do a face launch.
zh: 所以这就是为什么我们做的每个产品都做一个 face launch(分阶段发布)。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is a pilot.
zh: 第一个是试点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal of the pilot is to prove the accuracy, prove the quality, right?
zh: 试点的目标是证明准确性，证明质量，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You get your top, you know, AI native folks in the organization who are eager to work with you, give you feedback, improve the product, make sure that you got the rough edges through that, right?
zh: 你把组织里最顶尖的、渴望与你合作、给你反馈、改进产品的那帮 AI 原生的人拉进来，确保你通过他们磨平了那些粗糙的边缘，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after a couple of weeks, you come to a point where it looks like, okay, those rough edges are more smoother now, okay?
zh: 然后几周之后，你到达一个节点，看起来，好，那些粗糙的边缘现在更平滑了，好吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you go into your beta launch.
zh: 然后你进入 beta 发布阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do a 10% beta, right, with 600 people.
zh: 我们做 10% 的 beta,对吧,600 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There you are looking at do I truly have basically a minimum viable product?
zh: 那时你要看的是,我真的有一个最小可行产品吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the MVP really there?
zh: MVP 真的成立了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what will happen is that you will start getting tons of requests.
zh: 接下来会发生的是,你会开始收到海量的请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you connect this data?
zh: 你能接上这个数据吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you connect that data and everything?
zh: 你能接上那个数据吗,诸如此类?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you are looking at where are actually the concentrations happening?
zh: 然后你要看的是,这些需求实际上在哪里集中出现?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that means that if you don't get those things in, you don't truly have an MVP.
zh: 因为这意味着,如果你不把这些东西接入,你就没有真正的 MVP。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it's not gonna work for their daily workflows.
zh: 那样它就无法适用于他们的日常工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at that stage, you're also trying to prove are they coming back?
zh: 然后到了这个阶段,你还要证明,他们会回来吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So the things that we've really tracked there is basically like, okay, how many questions they're asking and everything, but what is the retention rate?
zh: 所以我们真正追踪的指标,基本上是,好吧,他们问了多少问题之类的,但留存率是多少?

speaker: Unknown
en: So we exited, for example, that at like more than 70% retention rate that the weekly active users were coming back.
zh: 比如我们在那一阶段结束时,周活用户的回访留存率达到了 70% 以上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, now we're in a good place, right?
zh: 好了,现在我们处于一个好的位置,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have confidence on the accuracy, we have on the confidence of basically the coverage of the product we have, and people are coming back.
zh: 我们对准确性有信心,我们对产品的覆盖面基本上有信心,而且用户会回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, now let's go to GA, and then you launch to the GA.
zh: 好,现在我们进入 GA,然后你正式发布了 GA。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you have your next problem.
zh: 但接下来你有下一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that this is a technical conference, but this is also where a lot of these products fail.
zh: 我知道这是一个技术大会,但这也是很多产品失败的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically how do you derive change management.
zh: 基本上就是,你如何做好变革管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you launch your product, you're two weeks into the launch, and then you are here.
zh: 所以你发布了产品,发布后两周,然后你在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all your management is like disappointed or frustrated.
zh: 为什么数字这么低?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why aren't people using this?
zh: 为什么没人用这个?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are numbers that are very low?
zh: 为什么这些数字这么低?

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I show them this graph.
zh: 然后我给他们看这张图。

speaker: Unknown
en: I say that only 20% of your, basically, organization actually tried the product.
zh: 我说,你的组织里基本上只有 20% 的人真正试用过这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I cannot do anything, it's not the product's fault if people are not even taking five minutes to try the product, right?
zh: 我无能为力,如果人们连五分钟都不肯花来试用产品,那不是产品的错,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If they try it and if they don't come back, okay, that's my problem, right?
zh: 如果他们试用了,但没有回来,好吧,那是我的问题,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But if they don't try it, then we have another problem.
zh: 但如果他们根本没试用,那我们就有另一个问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first, and I've seen this with many, many sales organizations in my past life as well and so on, usually this is a couple of month process.
zh: 所以第一点,我在过去生涯中见过非常非常多的销售组织,通常这是一个持续几个月的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you significantly invest in basically change management, in activation.
zh: 然后你需要在变革管理和激活上大幅投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will spend 60, 70% of my time in sales meetings, giving demos, building dashboards to see which teams adapted, you know, shaming the managers whose team is actually doing good, getting sponsorship from sales leaders to basically like make sure that they, you know,
zh: 我会把 60%、70% 的时间花在销售会议上,做演示,搭建仪表盘来看哪些团队采用了,你知道的,让那些团队表现好的经理有面子,从销售负责人那里获得支持,基本上就是为了确保他们,你知道的,

speaker: Unknown
en: They push their people to try these things and so on and then ultimately that gets your blue line up and then your questions start coming up and then your focus can shift into, okay, how do I drive more depth, right?
zh: 他们推动自己的团队去试用这些东西等等,最终这让蓝线升上去,然后你的问题开始增多,然后你的重心就可以转移到,好,我如何驱动更深的深度,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to really, really emphasize this, because if you hadn't done this, we would probably be doing half of where we are today.
zh: 我想非常非常强调这一点,因为如果你没做这件事,我们今天可能只有一半的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very, very important part.
zh: 所以这是一个非常非常重要的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as engineers, if you spend all your effort, you want to have a good product, make sure that the activation and the change management is lined up, like post-launch of the product as well.
zh: 而作为工程师,如果你投入全部精力想做出好产品,那就要确保激活和变革管理在产品发布之后也排上日程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we run into another issue.
zh: 现在我们遇到了另一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, you are, let's say that, four to six months down the run, right?
zh: 好,你,比如说,跑到第四到六个月了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens is you successfully launch the product, you're first rock stars in the company.
zh: 发生的情况是,你成功发布了产品,你成了公司里的第一批明星。

speaker: Unknown
en: People literally show you on the corridor like, hey, your product is awesome, we can talk to our data now, we don't need to wait on the queue to get access to analysts to answer our questions in every two weeks and so on.
zh: 人们在走廊上直接对你说,嘿,你的产品太棒了,我们现在可以直接和我们的数据对话了,我们不用再排队等分析师每两周才回答我们的问题了,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after a couple of months, they start coming back to you with frustrations.
zh: 而几个月后,他们开始带着不满回来找你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, I cannot do this in the product anymore.
zh: 嘿,我没法在产品里做这个了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw this other AI product that does this and so on.
